correctness.rationale: For each complete phase cycle, the clockwise gap moves d→d+U→d+U−V with fresh independent Bernoulli(q) indicators. Exact direct transitions verify both boundary absorb rules; the full-lazy-walk coupling differs by at most O(n) expected macrosteps, and its centered increments have variance 2pq. Donsker first-exit convergence plus a maximal-inequality clock law with mean n/p+O(1) yields generator p²q∂xx and the cubic scaling. Solving the boundary ODE gives the claimed complete Laplace transform. The optimal p and moments follow by differentiation/time scaling. An independent full pair-state discounted calculation for n≤80 numerically corroborates the proposed constant but is not used for proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary result, Gusev (arXiv:1404.6731, Section 3), solves first-moment recurrences for Bernoulli random inputs to Černý pair automata, but does not state or establish convergence of the whole rescaled hitting-time distribution, the Brownian Laplace law across all interior starting gaps, or limiting quantile-optimal bias. A separate same-object variance calculation determines only two moments at the fair bias; it does not imply the Laplace transform or weak limit. Gonze--Jungers (arXiv:1410.4034) treats a game-theoretic synchronizing-probability function and deterministic triple rendezvous, not random-word pair coalescence. Exact cycle reduction plus uniform clock control are needed. Full earlier coverage cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper or alternate process-limit formulation could already imply the result.
Gusev gives an explicit pair automaton, making the diffusion result a possible derivation from known transition structure; a prior unpublished limit could exist.
Direct finite-n numerical convergence is indicative, not proof or independence.

value.rationale: This is a distribution-level classification of synchronization noise for the canonical slow synchronizer over all fixed biased input laws and all macroscopic starting gaps. It quantifies tail/quantile behavior beyond the known mean and fair-input second-moment profiles, identifies an explicit first-exit universality class, and shows that the same nontrivial letter bias optimizes the entire limiting latency distribution, not merely the expectation. The result requires a two-boundary cycle decomposition and stochastic time change; it is not a direct substitution into a textbook single-chain formula.
